arxiv-1910-09721.title: Intelligence via ultrafilters: structural properties of some intelligence comparators of deterministic Legg-Hutter agents
arxiv-1910-09721.creator: \name Samuel Allen Alexander \email samuelallenalexander@gmail.com
arxiv-1910-09721.description: Abstract Legg and Hutter, as well as subsequent authors, considered intelligent agents through the lens of interaction with reward-giving environments, attempting to assign numeric intelligence measures to such agents, with the guiding principle that a more intelligent agent should gain higher rewards from environments in some aggregate sense.

arxiv-2306-08553.title: Noise Stability Optimization for Finding Flat Minima: A Hessian-based Regularization Approach
arxiv-2306-08553.creator: Hongyang R. Zhang ho.zhang@northeastern.edu, Dongyue Li li.dongyu@northeastern.edu, Haotian Ju ju.h@northeastern.edu
arxiv-2306-08553.description: Abstract The training of over-parameterized neural networks has received much study in recent literature. An important consideration is the regularization of over-parameterized networks due to their highly nonconvex and nonlinear geometry. In this paper, we study noise injection algorithms, which can regularize the Hessian of the loss, leading to regions with flat loss surfaces.

arxiv-2404-05267.title: Deforming Locally Convex Curves into Curves of Constant k k -order Width
arxiv-2404-05267.creator: Laiyuan Gao Horst Martini Deyan Zhang
arxiv-2404-05267.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Laiyuan Gao Horst Martini Deyan Zhang. Abstract A nonlocal curvature flow is introduced to evolve locally convex curves in the plane. It is proved that this flow with any initial locally convex curve has a global solution, keeping the local convexity and the elastic energy of the evolving curve, and that, as the time goes to infinity, the curve converges to a smooth, locally convex curve of constant k -order width.

arxiv-2501-02723.creator: Konrad Deka, Dominik Kwietniak, Bo Peng, Marcin Sabok
arxiv-2501-02723.description: Abstract . We show that Rufus Bowen’s Problem 32 on the classification of symbolic systems with the specification property does not admit a solution that would use concrete invariants. To this end, we construct a class of symbolic systems with the specification property and show that the conjugacy relation on this class is too complicated to admit such a classification.

arxiv-2503-09566.title: TPDiff: Temporal Pyramid Video Diffusion Model
arxiv-2503-09566.creator: Lingmin Ran, Mike Zheng Shou
arxiv-2503-09566.description: Abstract The development of video diffusion models unveils a significant challenge: the substantial computational demands. To mitigate this challenge, we note that the reverse process of diffusion exhibits an inherent entropy-reducing nature. Given the inter-frame redundancy in video modality, maintaining full frame rates in high-entropy stages is unnecessary.

pmc-11461637.description: Pampus argenteus is a highly commercial marine fish whose population is declining sharply. pmc-12620594.title: Adopting an Integrative and Co-Design Process to Contextualize Management Capacity Building in Hospitals
pmc-12620594.creator: Zhanming Liang, Hui Zhang
pmc-12620594.description: IntroductionContext plays a critical role in shaping how interventions are designed and implemented, and must therefore be considered prior to implementation. There is consensus that the relationship between contextual factors and intervention outcomes is best understood using qualitative and quantitative methods, the process for considering and incorporating context remains unclear.

pmc-13222452.title: Improving udder health in crossbred cows in New Zealand using Scandinavian Red sires
pmc-13222452.creator: Hamed Amirpour-Najafabadi, Craig McKimmie, Pavithra Ariyarathne, Hossein Alizadeh, Jonathan Hickford
pmc-13222452.description: Objectives: To test whether Scandinavian Red (SR) sires improve udder health (somatic cell score; SCS) in New Zealand crossbred dairy cows without compromising milk solids yield.Materials and Methods: Herd-test records (one test day per cow) from six pasture-based New Zealand herds were analyzed (n = 5,294).

pmc-13230727.title: CellTarget: a convex optimisation approach to discover cellular objectives
pmc-13230727.creator: Mariana Monteiro, James Morrissey, Cleo Kontoravdi
pmc-13230727.description: Metabolic network models are widely used in systems and synthetic biology to study cellular metabolism from microbes to mammals. However, their application to mammalian cells remains limited by the scarcity of intracellular flux measurements relative to network size. As a result, mammalian metabolic models are typically underdetermined and require optimisation-based assumptions to be solved.

pmc-13406207.title: FTO in Bone Diseases: Functions, Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential
pmc-13406207.creator: Haochuan You, Yixiang Zhao, Xiuyuan Wang, Haotian He, Dacheng Zhao, Yayi Xia
pmc-13406207.description: Skeletal homeostasis relies on coordinated interactions among osteoblasts, osteoclasts, osteocytes, chondrocytes, and bone marrow stromal cells. Disruption of this balance contributes to the development of osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, impaired skeletal repair, and bone malignancies. Fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO), an RNA demethylase that removes N6-methyladenosine (m6A) and related RNA modifications, has emerged as a key context-dependent regulator of skeletal biology.

pmc-13623077.title: Recent Studies on the Effectiveness and Safety of Anti-Obesity Medications: A Scoping Review
pmc-13623077.creator: Irma Melyani Puspitasari, Dimas Setyadi Putra, Alifa Nisa Deliyana, Nurqisthi Iqlima Adiputri, Lily Indriani Octovia, Sekar Ayu Paramita, Rano Kurnia Sinuraya
pmc-13623077.description: Obesity remains a major global public health challenge associated with increased morbidity, mortality, and reduced quality of life, necessitating effective treatment strategies beyond lifestyle modifications. The present scoping review aimed to synthesize recent evidence on the effectiveness and safety of anti-obesity medications (AOMs).

pmc-7616809.title: Virtual Reality for Preprocedure Planning of Covered Stent Correction of Superior Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defects
pmc-7616809.creator: Natasha Stephenson, Eric Rosenthal, Matthew Jones, Shujie Deng, Gavin Wheeler, Kuberan Pushparajah, Julia A. Schnabel, John M. Simpson
pmc-7616809.description: BACKGROUND:Covered stent correction (CSC) of a superior sinus venosus atrial septal defect is an alternative to surgery in selected patients, but anatomic variation means that assessment for CSC requires a 3-dimensional anatomic understanding. Heart VR is a virtual reality (VR) system that rapidly displays and renders multimodality imaging without prior image segmentation.
